final_result.reason: Revised to fix high-Tg and reactivity issues. Monomer1 is a flexible diglycidyl (two epoxide rings: substrings C1OC1 and C2OC2) connected by ether-rich triethylene glycol linkers to lower Tg (adds flexibility/ether character) while providing two epoxy reactive sites to raise crosslinking potential. Monomer2 is a flexible polyamine (triethylenetetramine-like, contains multiple NC motifs at least twice) providing multiple nucleophilic N sites to react with the epoxides, increasing crosslink-supporting reactive site density and thus Er. Aromatic/rigid fragments from the previous design were removed to reduce predicted Tg toward the 80 °C target while keeping sufficient functionality to approach Er ≈ 50. This combination preserves epoxy–amine compatibility and increases crosslink density versus the prior design.

result.reason: Monomer1 is a para-bis(oxiran-2-ylmethyl)benzene-type diglycidyl ether (two oxirane rings shown as C1OC1 and C2OC2) providing at least two epoxide reactive sites and an aromatic core to raise Tg and crosslink rigidity. Monomer2 is m-xylylenediamine (1,3-bis(aminomethyl)benzene) with two primary amine termini (NC motifs appear twice) that will efficiently cure epoxides via epoxy-amine chemistry. The combination yields a moderately high Tg (~80°C target) from the rigid aromatic units and a moderate-to-high crosslink density (Er ≈ 50 MPa target) from the difunctional epoxy + difunctional amine network. Both SMILES are synthetically plausible and satisfy the required functional-group and reactivity constraints.

The epoxy (C1OC1/C2OC2) ↔ amine (NC) pair ensures compatibility; removing the aromatic unit addresses the high Tg error and the multifunctional amine increases network functionality to raise Er toward the target.
